rationale: C02 is a concrete and material drafting template for the child. Both letters submit an atomic-information cooperation agreement under Section 123, define the same three permitted defense uses in the same numbered sequence, impose closely parallel transfer and security restrictions, make the same statutory risk determination, approve the agreement, authorize its execution, and direct Defense with Atomic Energy Commission assistance to communicate Restricted Data. The child adapts this machinery from NATO to Australia and adds provisions appropriate to bilateral reciprocal exchange. C17 shares the recipient and atomic-energy context but no operative template; C05 supplies only general security concepts and terminology.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Pursuant to Section 123 of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, I hereby submit to the Joint Committee on Atomic Energy a proposed agreement between the Governments of the United States and Australia for cooperation regarding communication of atomic information
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Pursuant to Section 123 of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, I hereby submit to the Joint Committee on Atomic Energy a proposed agreement for cooperation regarding the communication of atomic information to the North Atlantic Treaty Organization.
shared_material.explanation: Nearly identical statutory submission formula and description of the proposed agreement, with the recipient changed.

shared_material.child_excerpt: (1) the development of defense plans; (2) the training of personnel in the employment of and defense against atomic weapons; and (3) the evaluation of the capabilities of potential enemies in the employment of atomic weapons.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: (1) the development of defense plans; (2) the training of personnel in the employment of and defense against atomic weapons; and (3) the evaluation of the capabilities of potential enemies in employment of atomic weapons.
shared_material.explanation: The distinctive three-part enumeration is reproduced essentially verbatim and in the same order.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Atomic information made available pursuant to the proposed agreement will not be transferred to unauthorized persons, or beyond the jurisdiction of the recipient government
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Atomic information made available pursuant to the proposed agreement will not be transferred to unauthorized persons or beyond the jurisdiction of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization
shared_material.explanation: The child adapts the same nontransfer restriction to a bilateral recipient-government framework.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Accordingly, I hereby determine that the performance of this proposed agreement will promote and will not constitute an unreasonable risk to the common defense and security, and approve this agreement.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Accordingly, I hereby determine that its performance will promote and will not constitute an unreasonable risk to the common defense and security, and approve the proposed agreement for cooperation.
shared_material.explanation: The formal statutory determination and approval clause is materially identical.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I hereby authorize, subject to the provisions of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, the Secretary of State to execute the proposed agreement and the Department of Defense, with the assistance of the Atomic Energy Commission, to cooperate with Australia and to communicate Restricted Data to Australia under the agreement.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hereby authorize, subject to the provisions of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, the Honorable George W. Perkins ... to execute the proposed agreement and the Department of Defense, with the assistance of the Atomic Energy Commission, to cooperate with the North Atlantic Treaty Organization and to communicate Restricted Data to that Organization under the agreement.
shared_material.explanation: The child retains the same execution authorization and interagency implementation machinery while substituting the appropriate signatory and partner.
